passages.english: Every high priest is appointed from among men to represent them in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.

lines.text: Every high priest is chosen from among the people — chosen by God.
This high priest represents the people before God — as their mediator.
The high priest offers gifts to God.
And the high priest offers sacrifices to God for sins.

passages.english: He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and misguided, since he himself is beset by weakness.

lines.text: The high priest himself is weak.
So, being weak, the high priest has natural empathy with others who are weak.
Through this empathy, the high priest can be gentle and merciful to the weak.
So the high priest can deal gently with those whose weakness is ignorance.
And the high priest can also deal gently with those who in their weakness go astray.

passages.english: That is why he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.

lines.text: So the high priest must offer sacrifices for his own sins.
The high priest must also offer sacrifices for the people's sins.

passages.english: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.

lines.text: No one takes the honor of being high priest for himself.
God must call him to it.
God called Aaron the same way — Aaron, the first high priest.

passages.english: So also Christ did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest, but He was called by the One who said to Him: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”

lines.text: God is the One who said to Jesus:
"You are My Son."
"Today I have become Your Father."
God gave Jesus the honor of being high priest.
So, just like Aaron, Christ did not give Himself this honor.

passages.english: And in another passage God says: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

lines.text: Melchizedek was an ancient king who was also a priest of God.
His priesthood is far older than Aaron's — it existed long before Israel had any priests.
In another part of Scripture, God says to Christ:
"You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek."
So Christ is our great high priest — of the order of Melchizedek, not of Aaron.

passages.english: During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.

lines.text: During the days of Jesus' earthly life, He offered up prayers and urgent pleas.
Jesus prayed with loud cries and tears.
Jesus prayed to God, the One who could save Him from death.
And God heard Him, because of His deep reverence.

passages.english: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.

lines.text: Even though Jesus was the Son of God — God over all — He humbled Himself to the lowest place of all.
Jesus — our Master — became the servant of all, the lowliest of servants — giving Himself wholly to serve everyone and to obey God.
A son is greater than a servant, and yet the Son of God learned obedience through what He suffered — obeying God as a servant, no matter the pain it cost.
Jesus lived by every word of God, enduring all agony until all was accomplished.
Jesus was obedient even to death — death on a cross.
He always obeyed God perfectly, so He deserved the highest blessings — yet instead He became a curse for us, hanging on that wooden cross.

passages.english: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him and was designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek.

lines.text: And so Jesus was made perfect — though always perfectly free of sin, through His suffering, death and resurrection, He was made perfectly complete.
This is why Jesus became the source of eternal salvation.
He saves all who obey Him.
God designated Jesus as our high priest.
Jesus is a priest in the order of Melchizedek — an ancient priest of God.

passages.english: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you are dull of hearing.

lines.text: There is much to say about Christ our high priest, and about Melchizedek.
But those who received this letter had become slow to listen and understand.
So it was hard to explain these things to them.

passages.english: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to reteach you the basic principles of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food!

lines.text: These believers have followed Christ for a long time now.
So by now, these believers should already be teachers themselves.
But instead, they still need someone to teach them God's basic truths again.
These believers are like infants who can only drink milk.
This milk is the first teaching new believers begin with — turning from sin and trusting Christ.
These believers were not ready for solid food.
Solid food is the deeper teaching for the mature — those trained to tell good from evil.

passages.english: For everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness.

lines.text: Anyone who still lives on spiritual milk is only a spiritual infant.
Spiritual infants are not yet skilled in the message of righteousness — God's teaching about living rightly.

passages.english: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.

lines.text: Let us seek and obey God's will, again and again, until it becomes our way of life.
And then we will be training our senses the same way an athlete trains to win a race.
In time, we will grow skilled at telling good from evil.
So we become spiritually mature, ready to receive spiritual solid food — God's deeper teaching.
